CourseLatchBack to the story ↗
BUILD NOTES / HONEST BY DESIGN

One complete recovery.
Clear about what’s real.

CourseLatch is a focused recovery prototype for a paid course that stays locked. It joins the payment to the purchased access, asks the merchant to approve a specific correction, and checks the learner’s outcome.

This public site is a browser simulation.

Records are fictional, specialist consultations are scripted, and checkout moves no money. The working server and integration adapters are in the project source. PayPal sandbox, live AI, and Render accounts have not been configured or tested end to end.

Try three different outcomes

  1. A · Correct payment, missing access. Investigate, rehearse, approve, apply, and verify. Then open Maya’s first lesson. During rehearsal, the original stays locked.
  2. B · Wrong order reference. A matching price cannot prove the purchase. The case stops and access stays locked.
  3. C · Verification read fails once. Access is granted, but the case remains open. Retry the reads and watch the write count stay at one.

What the specialists contribute

Ledger checks payment evidence. Relay traces the failed handoff without inventing its cause. Patch proposes the smallest access correction. Prism challenges contradictions and checks the outcome. Expand their findings to inspect the original records. The optional model adapter uses four separate, role-specific consultations; it cannot execute repairs.

From sample to sandbox

  1. Run the server. The source includes a Node 24 application with SQLite persistence and an independently checked lesson-access endpoint. Run npm ci, npm test, then npm start.
  2. Configure PayPal sandbox. Add sandbox client credentials to the server environment. Unlock the developer session, restart the story, and use the optional PayPal sandbox button. The server creates and captures the order, then deliberately fails its own access update.
  3. Configure AI review. Add an OpenAI API key and a Structured Outputs-compatible Responses model. The interface labels model-generated findings distinctly. Invalid or incomplete output fails visibly.
  4. Run Render Workflows. Deploy the Node backend and workflow entry point. Configure the shared workflow secret and exact task slugs. Investigation finishes before approval. Approval starts a separate correction-and-verification run.

Detailed environment instructions, provider references, and acceptance checks are in docs/SETUP.md in the project source. Hosting the Node service and running provider integrations may incur charges. This build has not provisioned those services.

What has been checked

The automated suite covers isolated rehearsal, mismatched purchase fields, stale approval, repeat repairs, failed verification, session isolation, origin enforcement, operator gating, and mocked provider calls. Mocked tests support the implementation; they do not replace real sandbox and workflow acceptance tests.

What still needs real-world evidence

The project includes a five-seller interview kit. Ask about the last actual incident, the records they checked, its frequency, their existing workaround, and what would make a supervised trial credible. No interviews have been conducted and no demand or revenue claims are made.

A production version also needs a real course-platform connector, merchant and learner identity, verified webhook handling, shared transactional storage, retention controls, and refund-related access policies. This prototype is intentionally limited to one fictional course and one correction type.

The three-minute story

Start with the locked learner. Investigate the evidence. Rehearse while the learner remains locked. Approve one exact grant. Verify and open the lesson. Finish by showing the conflicting-payment stop and the failed-read retry. If live integrations are configured, show actual PayPal capture and Render run records alongside the result.
